settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: ConfigurationInterpolator javadoc states no Lookup objects are registered by default on a new instance (lines 61-69); the default set is supplied via DefaultLookups/DefaultStringLookup population (lines 103-121), so use of the default set is required.
Interpolation only occurs when application code calls interpolate()/resolve(); reading a raw value without interpolation does not trigger lookups (javadoc lines 72-77).

The actual side effects live in Commons Text string-lookup implementations, not in this repository's code, so impact depends on the dependency version and environment (not verified in the read spans).
candidates.description: ConfigurationInterpolator builds the static DEFAULT_PREFIX_LOOKUPS map from every DefaultLookups enum constant and adds the Commons Text DefaultStringLookup entries (ConfigurationInterpolator.java:103-121). DefaultLookups includes DNS (line 97, StringLookupFactory dnsStringLookup), SCRIPT (line 149, ScriptStringLookup) and URL (line 162, UrlStringLookup). Because these are registered as prefixes of the form ${prefix:name}, any configuration value that is interpolated can trigger a lookup whose implementation performs DNS resolution, remote URL retrieval, or script execution. The interpolator is the standard mechanism attached to configuration objects, so this code path is reachable whenever application code interpolates values that may have been influenced externally. This is the class of behavior addressed upstream in the 2.8 line; in this 2.7-SNAPSHOT tree the SCRIPT/DNS/URL entries are still present.
missing_evidence: The body of ConfigurationInterpolator.interpolate/resolve beyond line 200 (line 557 total) was not read, so the exact substitution call chain is unverified.
No evidence that untrusted input in this deployment flows into interpolation (no callers read).
pom.xml dependency versions for commons-text were not confirmed within the read range (lines 1-60 only).
preconditions: A configuration value containing a ${script:...}, ${dns:...} or ${url:...} expression is interpolated by org.apache.commons.configuration2.interpol.ConfigurationInterpolator.
The interpolated string content is influenced by an untrusted source (e.g., a loaded configuration file or externally supplied property).
The Commons Text version on the classpath provides the scripting/DNS/URL lookups and the relevant engine/dependencies are present.
candidates.title: Default interpolation lookups register script/DNS/URL prefixes enabling side-effecting variable expansion

counter_evidence: XMLConfiguration allows an application to inject a fully pre-configured DocumentBuilder through setDocumentBuilder (lines 336-347), which can eliminate the risk; a hardened builder is the documented workaround.
The default DefaultEntityResolver (line 240) is intended to resolve known entities and may restrict resolution, but its implementation was not read.

The createDocumentBuilder() body (expected around XMLConfiguration.java:850-890) was NOT successfully read in this review; it is therefore unknown whether secure-processing or entity features are set there.
candidates.description: XMLConfiguration.load(InputSource) obtains a DocumentBuilder via createDocumentBuilder() and calls builder.parse(source) (XMLConfiguration.java:1025-1026). The class stores a default entity resolver, new DefaultEntityResolver() (XMLConfiguration.java:240), and the createDocumentBuilder() snippet found via search uses a plain DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() with optional validating/schema settings and then result.setEntityResolver(this.entityResolver). Within the read span (XMLConfiguration.java:180-379 and 900-1050) no call to factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING), disallow-doctype-decl, or external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities disabling is visible. XMLDocumentHelper likewise creates a builder from DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() for new documents (lines 110-118) and, for source documents, retains the DOCTYPE public/system IDs (lines 139-157) while copying the document (lines 155-156). If a configuration XML file is attacker-controlled, a DOCTYPE with entity definitions may be processed during parsing.
missing_evidence: The actual createDocumentBuilder() method body was not read (the read attempt returned 'Tool is not available for this condition'), so feature settings are unverified.
resolver/DefaultEntityResolver and the resolver package were not read; whether it blocks external/parameter entities is unknown.
DefaultXMLDocumentBuilder / builder XMLBuilderParametersImpl defaults were not read.
No evidence that any XML input in a real deployment is attacker-controlled.
preconditions: An application loads an XML configuration from a source whose content can be influenced by an attacker (file, stream, URL).
The application relies on the default DocumentBuilder setup (no custom hardened DocumentBuilder passed via setDocumentBuilder, XMLConfiguration.java:345-347).
The underlying JAXP parser expands general/parameter entities and does not itself reject the DOCTYPE.
candidates.title: XMLConfiguration / XMLDocumentHelper parse XML with default DocumentBuilderFactory (DTD/entity handling not hardened in read span)
